intro: If you've been stepping over a tired bath or squeezing around a cramped shower tray in your Borthwickrow home, a wet room installation could be exactly what your bathroom needs. Wet rooms have moved well beyond a design trend — they're a practical, long-lasting solution that works particularly well in older homes where space can be awkward and original layouts weren't built with modern comfort in mind. Whether you're planning ahead for accessibility, adding genuine value to your property, or simply want a bathroom that looks and functions beautifully, getting the right installation done properly from the start makes all the difference.
localContext: Borthwickrow sits in the heart of Midlothian, and the properties here reflect that — a mix of solid older stone-built homes, period cottages with thick walls and character-filled layouts, alongside more recent modern estate builds. Each of these property types comes with its own set of considerations when planning a wet room. Stone-built and period cottages in Borthwickrow often have uneven floors, limited subfloor depth, and older plumbing runs that need updating before any wet room work begins. Modern estate homes tend to be more straightforward, but ceiling heights and partition walls can still vary. Borthwickrow sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring in when choosing your finishes and drainage. Limescale can build up on screens, fittings, and drainage channels over time, so choosing quality fixtures and considering a water softener as part of the wider project is genuinely sensible planning rather than an upsell.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Borthwickrow isn't a weekend job — it's a skilled, multi-stage project that typically takes between five and ten working days depending on the size of the room and what's being replaced or upgraded. The process starts with a full assessment of your existing bathroom, including floor structure, drainage position, and the current state of any plumbing or electrics. In older stone-built or cottage properties this survey stage is especially important, as floors sometimes need reinforcing or levelling before tanking can begin. Tanking is the waterproofing layer applied across the entire floor and lower walls — it's the most critical part of the job and should never be cut short. Once the tanking is fully cured, the floor is graded to slope towards the drain, tiles are laid, and the drainage channel or point drain is fitted flush to the surface. Plumbing connections for the shower, any thermostatic valve, and a fixed or handheld head are then made good. Electrics are handled by a qualified Part P registered electrician, either as part of the team or brought in separately. Finally, fixtures, screens or return panels if you're using them, and any finishing touches like heated towel rails or recessed niching are completed. You should expect some disruption, but a well-organised team will leave you with a functioning result that's genuinely built to last.
pricing: Wet room installations in Borthwickrow typically run between £6,000 and £12,000 for a full project. The lower end reflects a smaller, straightforward modern property with good existing drainage and minimal structural prep. Older stone-built homes and period cottages in Borthwickrow often sit toward the higher end due to floor preparation, extended tanking requirements, and the need to reroute older plumbing. The size of the room, quality of tiles and fixtures chosen, and whether you're adding features like underfloor heating or a bespoke drainage channel will all shift the final figure. Always get a detailed written quote before any work begins.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickrow and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for a project like this. Someone familiar with local property types will understand the quirks of stone-built construction, know what to expect beneath the floors of period cottages, and be able to plan realistically rather than discovering problems mid-job. Availability for follow-up visits is also easier when your installer isn't travelling from the other side of Edinburgh. A local professional also has a reputation to maintain within the community — in a smaller town like Borthwickrow, word travels fast, and that accountability tends to reflect in the quality of work delivered.

faqs.q: Can my period cottage in Borthwickrow actually accommodate a wet room?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes — but it requires careful planning. Older stone-built and cottage properties often have solid or uneven floors that need levelling before tanking. A good installer will assess this during the survey stage and give you an honest view of what's involved. These properties can end up with stunning wet rooms; the preparation just takes a little more care.

faqs.q: How does the moderately hard water in Borthwickrow affect my wet room long-term?
faqs.a: Hard water causes limescale to build up on tiles, glass screens, and drainage fittings over time. Choosing matte or textured tiles rather than highly polished surfaces can help disguise early build-up. Fitting a quality thermostatic valve with descaling-friendly internals is also wise. Some homeowners in Borthwickrow add a water softener at the same time, which protects the whole installation and reduces maintenance.

faqs.q: How long will the installation take and will I be without a bathroom?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Borthwickrow take between five and ten working days. You'll be without a functioning bathroom during this time, so it's worth planning ahead — whether that's a temporary shower arrangement or timing the work to suit your household. A good installer will give you a realistic daily schedule so you're never left guessing about progress.

faqs.q: Is underfloor heating worth adding to a wet room in Borthwickrow?
faqs.a: Given Midlothian winters, underfloor heating in a wet room is a popular addition and genuinely worth considering. It keeps the floor warm underfoot, helps the room dry out more quickly after use, and reduces the damp atmosphere that can affect grout and seals over time. Adding it during the initial installation is always far more cost-effective than retrofitting it later.
